notes: Walks the checked CEL AST to collect literal placeholder names and flags non-literal ones as dynamic. Only response placeholders (status_code/text, header.*, upstream latency) or dynamic names make a set response-based, which matches the agreed spec and the reference. Thorough table tests cover the shorthand, ph(), literals, near-miss names and concatenation, plus an end-to-end no-retry test.

Matches the reference approach: it walks the checked CEL AST for literal `ph()` placeholder names and treats non-literal names as dynamic, then retries on the response only when an exact response placeholder or the `header.` prefix is present; the unit and integration tests cover every maintainer-specified case (shorthand vs `ph()`, escaped literals, `status_codes`, `upstream.host`, dynamic names, plus pass-through of the 200 response and body).

Correctly stops expanded callers from being written straight to cancelled: it re-reads each caller and re-aggregates it from its children, falls back to cancelOneJob for unexpanded callers, and wakes the concurrency group after settling a run with no job updates. It adds an extra per-caller DB query and an emit condition broader than the reference's status-change check, but both are harmless; the nested-caller and force-cancel wake tests are focused and meaningful.

Fixes both root causes. Expanded callers are no longer force-written as cancelled: their status is re-aggregated from their children, with a fallback to the plain cancel when a caller is not expanded yet. Concurrency emission is added for force-cancels that only settle the run status. The `IsDone()` emit condition is slightly broader than the reference and arguably more robust. The extra child query and the redundant refresh are minor overhead, and the new tests cover the nested cancelling cascade and the emit-on-force-cancel path.

Both backends get the core behaviour right: symlinks are skipped unless --links is set, a notice names the flag, links are listed with the .rclonelink suffix, they read back their target and honour range/seek, NewObject agrees with List, and a member already named .rclonelink stays a regular file. It diverges from the reference by silently dropping any zip symlink that clashes with another entry, and by eagerly opening every zip symlink member at listing time, which costs extra reads on remote-backed archives. The clash dropping is the likely cause of the failing hidden test. The extra addLinks logic is complex and pokes at DirTree internals. The added zip and squashfs tests are thorough.

Implements --links handling for both zip and squashfs (log notice, .rclonelink naming, range and seek reads, NewObject agreeing with List), but the zip side reads every symlink target eagerly while listing, costing extra remote I/O on S3-hosted archives. It also adds a fairly complex clash-dropping pass that edits dirtree internals and silently drops symlinks the spec says should be listed; the hostile-archive case diverges from the reference and one hidden test fails, though the added tests are thorough.

The fix looks correct on reading: shared refcounted state owns one dup'd fd that is closed on last release, the unlink uses the real address, the CAS guard stops double release, and abstract sockets are never unlinked; but it rewrites internals the task did not require (the unixSockets map type, the unixListener/unixConn fields, deleteListener receivers), the package suite fails outright, and 0/7 hidden tests pass, most likely a compile break against tests written for the original types, despite its own thorough tests.

The shared-state redesign looks sound on review: a dedicated dup'd fd is closed by the last holder, the bound path is unlinked, a CAS guards double close, release runs under the lock, and abstract sockets are skipped; but replacing the unixSockets map type and removing the mapKey/count fields, plus converting deleteListener/deletePacketConn to pointer types, is a broad refactor that most likely breaks compilation against the expected internals, so 0/7 hidden tests pass and the package suite fails.

The core fix matches the reference: `Close` is added to the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect first, and `Reconnect` resets USM engine state only when the connection is closed; it also usefully clears `ContextEngineID` and the localized keys. However, the plugin defers the close until the end of the agent's gather rather than closing right after the failing request, so later tables keep using the stale session within the same gather. Tests are extensive, but the package suite failed, and the unrelated edit to `TestSnmpInitGosmi` is scope creep.

The core fix matches the spec and is sound: `Close()` is added to the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection, and reconnecting resets the USM engine ID, boots and time, and also clears `ContextEngineID`, a sensible extra reset; the deviations are that the deferred, flag-based close only takes effect after all tables in the gather (so later tables in the same gather still use the stale session), the `TestSnmpInitGosmi` path tweak is unrelated, and the package suite fails, likely in the candidate's own added network or recording tests.

Generalizes prefix stripping, adds the rename/copy fallback, and adds a builder helper that pins srcPrefix/dstPrefix/noprefix; it also forces mnemonicPrefix=false, which overrides the user's display preference where the reference deliberately keeps it, and it extends the fix to the stash-show|apply pipe, which is justified; the visible tests only update command-arg expectations and the parser tests are not visible in the truncated diff.

Fixes the bug the same way the reference does: it strips any single leading path component (keeping /dev/null), resolves paths from `rename to`/`copy to` lines, and adds a shared builder helper that forces a/ and b/ prefixes on every diff lazygit runs (including `stash show` and the `SaveStagedChanges` pipe into `git apply`). Unlike the reference, it also forces `diff.mnemonicPrefix=false`, which needlessly overrides the prefixes the user chose for displayed diffs. The `pathFromDiffGitLine` rewrite is cut off in the diff, so it is trusted on the strength of the passing hidden tests. The visible test changes only update expected argv lists.

The core approach matches the reference: it tracks the max exemplar timestamp, keeps the series in `gc` and `gcSeries` while that timestamp is at or after `minValidTime`, releases chunks for selected/stale compaction, and records exemplars on WAL and snapshot replay. However, it records the exemplar only at commit time, after the WAL write, so a concurrent GC can still drop a series whose exemplar is already in the WAL. It also leaves `series.app` set in ordinary `gc`, and it changes the internal `gc`/`gcSeries` signatures and the pending-commit bitmask, which breaks the hidden tests and fails the package suite.

The design is close to the reference: it keeps the series identity while an exemplar is at or after minValidTime, releases chunks and the appender in gcSeries, and records exemplar timestamps on WAL and snapshot replay. However, it records the exemplar only at commit rather than at AppendExemplar, so a series that gets an exemplar but no sample can be evicted before commit. It also leaves `series.app` set in the ordinary gc path, and it changes the signatures of the internal gc/gcSeries functions and steals a bit from the pending-commit counter, which likely broke the hidden tests (0/3) and the package suite.
